newsitem.title: MEXICO: Televisa applies to sell Cablevision stake.
newsitem.headline: Televisa applies to sell Cablevision stake.

text.p: Media company Grupo Televisa has set up a new subsidiary to control its 51 percent stake in cable television company Cablevision, which would enable it to transfer ownership to Telefonos de Mexico, according to a report sent by Televisa to the Federal Monopolies Commission (CFC), and obtained by Reuters.
The new firm, called Editora Factum, will also take charge of Televisa's transmissions in two channels in the Ultra High Frequency band.

"Within the corporate restructuring process under way at Televisa, the company set up Factum on May 7, 1996, in which it holds a 99.8 percent stake and has the sole aim of transferring its stake in Cablevision", the report to the CTC said.
Both Televisa and Telefonos de Mexico (Telmex) declined to comment on the subsidiary. Televisa operates Mexico's principal television network and Telmex is the country's largest telephone company.
Factum already has a 51 percent stake in Cablevision, which was formalized at a shareholder's meeting held May 8.

CFC sources told Reuters that the report constitutes just one of the first consultations that Televisa has brought up regarding transferral of its ownership of Cablevision stock to Sercotel, a subsidiary of telephone company Telmex.
Telmex currently has a 49 percent stake in Cablevision.
"The aim...is that Televisa should no longer participate alongside Telmex in the cable television market," the report says.
A spokesman for the Commission said that Televisa had not, however, formerly applied for approval of the sale of its stake in Cablevision to Telmex.
"The Commission has received nothing official from either Televisa or Telmex, there have only been prior consultations", said the spokesman, who did not want to be quoted by name.
Cablevision held a special shareholders' meeting on May 2 in which it was agreed to divide the company into two parts to enable Telmex and Televisa to separate their holdings.

One of the new companies, Satelital UHF, will control the concessions that Cablevision has requested from the Communications and Transport Ministry (SCT), to operate television broadcasting by ultra high frequency (UHF).
The other firm, Milar SA de CV, will operate cable television broadcasts.
Under the scheme proposed to the CTC, Televisa would no longer trade in cable television, but would still retain Cablevision's rights to broadcast in the UHF band.
